SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / COMFORT & INCLUSION

Strategies to boost employee well being in your company.

Design for a range of people and working needs. This Space Craft planning note looks at strategies to boost employee well being in your company through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTEAsk people what gets in the wayOffer sensible choicesKeep design in perspectiveMap activity before assigning desksBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Ask people what gets in the way

Invite input on distractions, access, comfort and the settings people cannot currently find. A workplace brief should allow different experiences to be heard.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Offer sensible choices

A combination of quiet settings, collaborative areas and comfortable shared space can support different tasks. Discuss lighting, sound and furniture with users and relevant specialists.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Keep design in perspective

A physical space can support everyday comfort, but it cannot replace healthy management practices or professional support. Avoid treating a finish, colour or layout as a guaranteed wellbeing outcome.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Map activity before assigning desks

Write down the tasks people perform, how often teams overlap and when visitors arrive. A desk count alone will not reveal the need for private calls, project tables or storage.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • Include different users in the brief.
  • Review accessibility throughout the journey.
  • Treat user feedback as a design input, not a promise of a measured outcome.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.
